bullets.title: June CPI/PPI both soft; Fed hike odds collapse to ~12% for July
bullets.body: June headline CPI fell -0.42% m/m (core -0.02% m/m, core y/y down to 2.6% from 2.9%); PPI came in at -0.28% headline vs 0.0% consensus, supercore PPI 0.13% vs 0.3% expected. July Fed hike odds fell from ~50% pre-print to ~12%; core PCE now tracking +0.17% m/m for June. Morgan Stanley notes disinflation is confirmed and expected to continue through year-end; tariff pass-through appears near complete.

bullets.title: US-Iran military strikes escalate; Strait of Hormuz supply risk pushes crude to ~$80/bbl
bullets.body: US CENTCOM launched strikes against Iran beginning at 6am ET, ending at 7:30am ET, targeting Iran's ability to attack commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. Iran's IRGC threatened to halt all regional oil and gas exports if US maintains military presence. WTI and Brent trading around $80/barrel on the escalation; National Security Advisor Hassett said Iran's ability to hold the global economy hostage is degraded.

bullets.title: BofA FMS: Investors price out recession; 54% see no-landing, sentiment most bullish since Feb
bullets.body: BofA's latest fund manager survey shows 54% of respondents expect a 'no landing' scenario (record high), only 2% expect a hard landing, and 83% see no Fed hike before midterms. Sentiment is the most bullish since February, reflecting fading tariff fears and softer inflation data.

bullets.title: Morgan Stanley Q2 equities trading $6.30B — 41% above $4.47B estimate; capital markets broadly strong
bullets.body: MS reported Q2 total revenue $21.35B vs $19.58B estimate; equities trading $6.30B smashed the $4.47B estimate. Wealth management NNAs grew 8.1% and revenues came in at $8.86B vs $8.68B est. Sector-wide bank theme: capital markets and fee income thriving (Wall Street beating Main Street), while deposit trends are softer; banks with Wall Street exposure outperforming.

bullets.title: NY State imposes 1-year moratorium on large data center permits (>50MW); broader regulatory risk emerging
bullets.body: Governor Hochul signed an executive order temporarily banning new large data center construction (>50MW) in New York for up to one year, citing need to establish better agreement structures. Approximately $156B of data center projects were already cancelled/delayed in 2025 and another $130B in 1Q26. Citi sees spillover risk to other states; WULF projects at Lake Mariner and Cayuga under scrutiny though existing construction reportedly unaffected.

bullets.title: Hyperscale AI capex cycle accelerating: MS raises 2027-2028 forecasts to $1.2T and $1.4T
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's Brian Nowak raised hyperscale capex forecasts to ~$1.2T in 2027 and ~$1.4T in 2028, driven by 4x AI capacity growth 2025-2028 with upward revisions across META, AMZN, and GOOGL. ASML raised FY26 revenue guidance to €43B-€45B (prior €36B-€40B) with gross margin lifting to 55%-57% vs prior 52%; logic capex expected +25% and memory +75% in 2026. UBS notes no evidence of curtailment in foundational model/infrastructure spend.

bullets.title: Goldman June HF Wrap: AI/growth underperformed in June; quants suffered worst week since Dec '23
bullets.body: S&P 500 delivered best quarterly performance in over 5 years in H1 2026. AI and growth-oriented names underperformed in June on valuation concerns; value sectors (healthcare, industrials, financials) outperformed. Small-caps on track for largest annual outperformance vs S&P 500 since 2003. Quant managers experienced most painful last 6 trading days since December 2023 on crowded trade unwinding and momentum reversals.

bullets.title: Empire Mfg hit 57.5 in July (ISM-adj); manufacturing expansion broad-based with easing price pressures
bullets.body: July Empire Manufacturing ISM-equivalent index rose to 57.5 from 53.4, with broad expansion in sub-components including capex plans, headcount, and demand. Prices paid fell more than prices received, widening margins. Tariff pass-through appears near completion; tracking July ISM Manufacturing PMI at 53.5.

bullets.title: China Q2 GDP slowed to 4.3% YoY — below consensus, lowest ex-Covid in decades; no stimulus expected
bullets.body: China's Q2 GDP growth decelerated to 4.3% from 5.0% in Q1, below consensus and the weakest reading outside of Covid. 22V notes the miss was not severe enough to trigger fresh stimulus; PBOC likely pursuing gradual H2 rate cuts. China's economy remains in a deleveraging malaise with chip exports providing the primary growth support; exports running +27% y/y in June gives policymakers room to tolerate weak domestic demand.

bullets.title: Warsh hawkish at House testimony; Fed signaling inflation still the priority despite soft prints
bullets.body: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh rejected the soft CPI as a 'mission accomplished' signal, reaffirming commitment to price stability. Waller took direct aim at the Trimmed Mean inflation measure as misleading. White House economic advisor Hassett countered, arguing economic data provides no justification for rate hikes and that Warsh will 'drive the Fed to the right answer.' Debate over Fed path intensifying heading into summer data.

bullets.title: Apple Intelligence gets China approval via Alibaba Qwen integration; JPM upgrades AAPL to Overweight
bullets.body: Chinese regulators approved Apple's on-device AI features for iPhones, iPads, Macs, and visionOS, with Alibaba's Qwen and Baidu's Ernie as partners — resolving a two-year regulatory delay. JPMorgan upgraded AAPL to Overweight, arguing Apple Intelligence will overcome iPhone 18 price elasticity concerns by driving upgrade differentiation. C3Q iPhone builds remain unchanged at 54M; C2Q builds at 52M showing better-than-seasonal performance.

bullets.title: NVDA GPU capacity on AWS unavailable/uneconomical; workloads shifting to Neoclouds (NBIS, CRWV)
bullets.body: Per MS TMT, NVDA GPU capacity on AWS is either unavailable or uneconomically priced, pushing AI startup workloads to Neocloud providers including Nebius (NBIS), CoreWeave (CRWV), and Together AI. NBIS simultaneously launched a new asset-light partnership model where infrastructure partners deploy its AI cloud platform with Nebius supplying systems architecture and software stack, taking capacity to market via its global sales organization.

bullets.title: Buffett confirms he personally initiated Berkshire's Google investment; regrets not buying earlier
bullets.body: Warren Buffett told CNBC he was the one who initiated Berkshire Hathaway's investment in Alphabet, and said he made a mistake not buying the stock earlier. He appeared live on CNBC during the morning session.

bullets.title: Stripe + Advent bid $60.50/share (~$53B) for PayPal; Block also contributing equity; board meeting July 20
bullets.body: Stripe and Advent International submitted a joint offer to acquire PayPal at $60.50/share (~28% premium, ~57% above 52-week low) with ~$50B in committed bank financing; Block (XYZ) contributing a small portion of ~$17B equity commitment. Combined Stripe+PayPal unbranded TPV would represent ~12-13% of US payment volume TAM. PayPal board meeting scheduled July 20; UBS maintains Neutral, notes anticompetitive risks from overlapping enterprise clients. Suspicious call volume ahead of announcement flagged to SEC.

bullets.title: Cybersecurity names (CRWD, PANW) surge ~7% on IBM CEO commentary about client cyber spending pause
bullets.body: IBM issued a rare negative pre-announcement citing large deal slippage, supply-chain capex shifts, and cybersecurity 'distractions,' sending IBM shares -25% (worst day on record). Paradoxically, CRWD and PANW rallied ~7% on the IBM CEO commentary which implied clients are pausing Z-mainframe spending and reallocating to cybersecurity. Citi sees 10-15% more downside for IBM to ~$190 PT.

bullets.title: NY datacenter moratorium + ASML capacity ramp complicate data center/semicap sector outlook
bullets.body: NY's one-year datacenter permit freeze adds near-term regulatory uncertainty for AI infrastructure while ASML's massive beat-and-raise (FY26 rev guidance to €43-45B from €36-40B, GM to 55-57%) confirms robust upstream chip demand. Intel confirmed using ASML High-NA EUV on 18A Panther Lake ahead of schedule. Samsung confirmed it has not received NVDA HBM4 volume orders, only evaluation samples.

bullets.title: Value-momentum rotation: hedge funds rotating out of AI/Korea; value proposed as momentum hedge
bullets.body: 22V Research notes momentum factor faces continued headwinds with historical max drawdown averaging -25% post -20% decline outside recessions. Name overlap between top-decile Momentum and Value at low end of historical range supports negative correlation. Goldman notes AI infrastructure stocks expected to account for ~50% of 2026 S&P EPS growth, but large-cap quality defensives (NVDA, AVGO, TXN) leading MTD while longer-duration growth semis lag.

bullets.title: FCC vote August 6 to repeal 39% TV ownership cap; enables deals for NXST, FOXA
bullets.body: FCC Chair Brendan Carr confirmed plans for an August 6 vote to eliminate the national TV ownership cap in favor of case-by-case review, removing a blanket prohibition on deals exceeding 39%. This clears the path for Nexstar/Tegna and other broadcast consolidation deals; bullish for NXST and FOXA.

bullets.title: Defense reconciliation bill scaled back to $60B from $350B; passage odds improved but still long shot
bullets.body: House Republicans released Reconciliation 3.0 with a $60B defense funding target (vs. Trump's $350B request), aligning with the Administration's $67B supplemental request. Wolfe DC Policy notes the narrower bill has better passage odds but faces major obstacles: dysfunctional House majority, Senate skepticism, and tight timeline with House recessing after next week. Senate action delayed until September at earliest; overall defense funding expected to be status quo.

bullets.title: US lodging RevPAR +5.2% for week ending 7/11; luxury +14.2%; 3Q tracking well ahead of consensus
bullets.body: US weekly RevPAR rose 5.2% Y/Y to $112 driven by World Cup host markets (+11.4%) and luxury chain-scale (+14.2%). 3Q26 tracking significantly above consensus: Hyatt +9.8% vs consensus +3.5%, MAR +8.2% vs +3.2%, HST +11.5% vs +2.2%, PK +12.3% vs +3.1%.
